entries.title: Word counts
entries.quote: The word count is the number of words in a document or passage of text.
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: word frequencies over a passage, section, book or UTF-8 file; exact normalized term counts by doctrine. Counts measure word occurrences, not concepts.

entries.title: Word tokenization
entries.quote: Typically, lexical tokenization occurs at the word level.
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: Unicode letters and marks with internal apostrophes, NFC and case folding. These word tokens differ from model subword tokens; SOL does not implement the Unicode default boundary algorithm.

entries.title: Relative frequencies and comparisons
entries.quote: The relative frequency is the ratio of absolute frequency to the sample size.
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: rates per 10,000 tokens, target-minus-reference rate differences and log2 rate ratios, with no smoothing. Empty denominators and absent words have explicit undefined measures. These are descriptive comparisons.

entries.title: Sentence segmentation and length
entries.quote: is the problem in natural language processing of deciding where sentences begin and end.
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: punctuation-rules-v1 segmentation, sentence lengths in word tokens and longest sentences. Human boundary validation remains open; the segmentation-pilot tools were removed in the 21 October cleanup.

further.title: A Maximum Entropy Approach to Identifying Sentence Boundaries

entries.title: Lexical distribution and source context
entries.quote: listing every instance of each word with its immediate context.
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: word results list every occurrence with the words around it, up to 1,000 per word. Occurrences past each passage’s first are found again at display time and not saved in the study. Exact lexical evidence does not identify philosophical concepts.

entries.title: Prose projection
entries.quote: plain text is a loose term for unformatted text or nontextual data represented as text
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: prose export selects eligible attributed main text and removes structural headings and images from feature text, retaining source metadata separately. This SOL-specific projection is more selective than plain-text conversion.

entries.title: TF-IDF
entries.quote: The tf–idf is the product of two statistics, term frequency and inverse document frequency.
entries.essence: Runs in ESSENCE: engine, CLI (sol essence tfidf) and the Experiment screen. The versioned tfidf-v1 method uses raw-count TF, smoothed natural-log IDF ln((1+N)/(1+df))+1 and document L2 normalization. Documents are word-provider passages, or one whole file; overall weights average all normalized document vectors. See Methods for scopes, limits and verification.

entries.title: Word vectors
entries.quote: In natural language processing, a word embedding is a representation of a word.
entries.essence: Reading topic; no word-vector model or adapter is bundled with ESSENCE.

further.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

entries.title: Transformers
entries.quote: the transformer is a family of artificial neural network architectures based on the multi-head attention mechanism
entries.essence: Reading topic; no Transformer model or adapter is bundled with ESSENCE.
